Dr Paul Lee has documented more than 5,500 reported hauntings around the country over a decade, including stories from across Teesside

Richard Ault

13:36, 30 Oct 2026

Phantom kitchen saboteurs, spectral soldiers, and Victorian children lingering in shopfronts are among thousands of apparitions reported to be haunting Britain’s towns and cities.

‌

‌

Author Dr Paul Lee has documented more than 5,500 reported hauntings around the country over a decade of painstaking research, and they are all included in our interactive map revealing Britain’s most haunted locations.

‌

Reports range from everyday oddities – including phantom tobacco smoke and unexplained footsteps – to intense poltergeist claims involving flying plates and airborne kitchen utensils.

‌

According to Dr Lee’s research, Britain’s most haunted postcode is the ME1 neighbourhood, which covers Rochester, Burham, and Wouldham in Kent.

York City Centre (YO1) is the UK’s second most haunted postcode, and is rightly famous for its ghost walks. One of the city's most chilling tales centres on St Saviour Church, where a "grey lady" is reputed to walk at midnight. Local folklore tells of an amateur ghost hunter who spent the night locked inside the church, only to be discovered the following morning either dead with his face a “mask of terror”, or scared out of his senses, depending on the retelling.

On Teesside, there a tales of ghostly goings on at Albert Park and in the Swatter's Carr. There are also stories from Middlesbrough Theatre, Preston Park and Redcar Central Hotel and many more.

‌

Since Dr Lee started his research, a handful of haunted buildings that he documented no longer exist. However, the spooks described may still linger on. You can discover the haunted locations near you using our interactive map.

‌

All the descriptions of paranormal activity on the map have come from Dr Lee’s meticulous research, which, in many cases, includes interviews with witnesses and his own investigations, during which he has visited numerous locations and trawled through various newspaper archives.

Dr Lee said: “Of course, some of the reports in the database could be hoaxes or urban legends; there is no way to know in many cases.” Dr Lee, who holds a doctorate in nuclear physics, began compiling the national register in 2015 and continues to update the archive.

His recent investigations include the Syderstone Ghost — a series of unexplained night-time disturbances in a Norfolk village that was recently featured in Fortean Times.

Dr Lee has published his findings in several volumes, including the UK Haunted Hospitality series, which investigates more than 2,000 haunted pubs, hotels, and eateries across the country. You can find out more about his research by visiting his website: www.paullee.com/ghosts .
